meta.title: 802 Universe — tools and notes from across the 802 standards
meta.description: A small collection of free tools, references and teardowns covering the IEEE 802 family: Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, fibre and network security.

hero.title: One family of standards. *Everything* runs on it.
hero.sub: Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, fibre, VLANs, port security — all of it grew out of the same committee. This is where I put the tools and notes I build while working across it.

about.heading: About
paragraphs: I'm Manish. I work at the hard end of networking — the problems that survive three tiers of troubleshooting and end up needing a capture, a timestamp, and a very careful reading of the standard.
Most of what's on this site started as something I built to answer one question faster, then kept because it turned out useful. If any of it saves you an afternoon, that's the whole point.

facts.label: Focus
facts.value: 802.11 — RF design, DFS, 6 GHz, packet analysis

tools.heading: Pick something and open it.
tools.note: Every tile is its own page or repository. Nothing here needs an account.

projects.title: Wireshark Profile Library
projects.desc: Ready-made Wireshark profiles across 20 protocol categories. Drop the folder in, restart, and the columns and colouring rules are already right.

projects.title: LogLens
projects.desc: A single HTML file that parses tech-support bundles in the browser. Nothing is uploaded anywhere — open the file, drop the log, read the summary.

projects.title: 802.11 Reference Workbook
projects.desc: Frame formats, information elements, timers and channel plans collected in one workbook, so the lookup takes ten seconds instead of ten minutes.

projects.title: 802.1X, End to End
projects.desc: What actually happens between supplicant, authenticator and RADIUS server — and the four places it usually breaks.

projects.title: Channel Planner
projects.desc: A visual channel-plan sketchpad for 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz — set your width, see the overlap, export the plan.
